content:
alex: spotted an odd duplicate-append bug in the onboarding stream example. Upload stream sends chunks with x-rw-replay-id + x-rw-replay-seq, but when auth refresh happens mid-chunk the retry path re-starts seq from 1 for the resumed chunk. Server sees (replay-id, seq=1) again and appends duplicate data.

alex: short repro: start upload(stream) -> chunk1 seq=1 sent -> 429 on chunk2 -> client retries chunk2 quickly (jitter ~40ms) -> auth auto-refresh finishes -> retry sends chunk2 with seq reset to 1 -> server appends both chunk1 and chunk2 as seq=1 duplicates.

alex: logs: 
```
2026-06-11T09:02:10Z INFO stream id=st-77 chunk=2 send start auth=refreshing
2026-06-11T09:02:10Z WARN 429 stream=st-77 backoff=40ms
2026-06-11T09:02:10Z INFO auth refreshed for user=77
2026-06-11T09:02:10Z INFO resend stream=st-77 headers=(authorization: Bearer new) seq=1 // expected seq=2
2026-06-11T09:02:10Z INFO server appended chunk seq=1 duplicate=true
```

nora: ouch. streaming seq reset is new to me. I thought replay-id + seq were generated at the API boundary and persisted through retries. Where is the seq state held?

chris: current JS transport keeps replay-id in req.meta and increments seq in a small per-connection counter that lives on the transport instance. When auth.refresh replaces the auth transport instance we end up resetting that counter. So replay-id survives but seq counter does not.

sam: two fixes: (1) move seq counter into the logical-request context (not transport instance) so auth refresh doesn't reset it, (2) ensure retry clones copy both replay-id and the current seq state. Also clarify server semantics: server should dedupe by (replay-id, seq) and accept idempotent chunk replacement semantics (replace if same seq already exists).

alex: proposed quick patch: create a small StreamContext object at stream start and attach to request ctx; StreamContext holds replayId and nextSeq; increment nextSeq for each chunk; retry clones copy StreamContext reference so seq keeps advancing even across refresh. Pseudo: 
```
// on stream start
const streamCtx = { replayId: uuid(), nextSeq: 1 };
req.ctx.stream = streamCtx;
// sending chunk
const seq = streamCtx.nextSeq++;
headers['x-rw-replay-id'] = streamCtx.replayId;
headers['x-rw-replay-seq'] = String(seq);
await auth.ensureValid(req.ctx);
await transport.sendChunk(chunk, { headers });
```

chris: will that handle resumed uploads where connection is severed and client restarts a new HTTP connection? We must persist StreamContext across resume attempts if they are the same logical stream. For true resume semantics we may need a small persisted session or pass the original replayId in resume token so server can match.

nora: server-side safety: accept idempotent chunk semantics. If server sees duplicate (replayId, seq) treat as no-op. If receives seq less-than-or-equal-to-lastSeen and content matches, treat as idempotent; if different content, raise error. We'll add TTL=30m for stream ids.

sam: good. also recommend a jitter/backoff change for streaming: prefer base backoff 120ms with jitter 0.5 for chunk retries to avoid overlapping typical auth refresh windows (~50-150ms). But streaming latency matters, so don't make it huge.

chris: will prepare node patch: (1) StreamContext per logical stream, (2) ensure retry clones copy ctx reference, (3) merge meta->headers on clones, (4) unit+integration test that fakes auth rotation mid-chunk and asserts no duplicate append.

alex: i'll open issue DEVEX-5850 and attach logs + harness. after node fix, we'll mirror minimal snippet for Go/Python: use context.WithValue(ctx, "rw.stream.ctx", ctxStruct) or thread-local per logical stream. Keep examples short.

dev-bot: created PR alex/stream-seq-context -> ci/presubmit queued (4 checks)

nora: small danger: ensure we don't reuse replayId across unrelated streams. Generate per-logical-stream and tie to user+operation id. Also document resume token mechanics for clients that persist state across process restarts.

sam: will add spec changes: x-rw-replay-id per logical stream/request, x-rw-replay-seq monotonic per stream, server dedupe rules, recommended backoff defaults for streams, and sample code for Node/Go/Python.

alex: temporary mitigation: update onboarding sampleapp to use backoff base=120ms jitter 0.5 for streaming chunk retries and add note about persistent stream contexts. Long-term: patch SDK + server dedupe TTL.

chris: adding test: start stream, force 429 on chunk2, simulate auth.refresh during retry, assert server got seq 2 (not 1) and no duplicate append.

nora: thanks. ping me for review, this hit a customer using the sampleapp's multipart uploader. :thumbsup:
